Getting started with weft

Source: vignettes/weft.Rmd
weft.Rmd

This article is for anyone who writes reports in R Markdown or Quarto and wants the numbers in the prose to come from the analysis. After it you will be able to turn weft on in a document, print computed values with formatters, choose wording from a value, check a value with claim(), and read the report weft gives when a check fails.

What weft adds

weft adds two things to the markdown you already write.

A value is inline R code. With no attribute block, `r x` prints exactly as knitr prints it. With an attribute block, `r x`{.num} prints through one of weft’s formatters.

A span is a bracket of prose with an attribute block that names a weft key: [a site | # sites]{n="k"}. The key’s R expression chooses which part of the bracket prints.

Both are ordinary Pandoc syntax. A value with an attribute block or a span with a weft key is a construct. The rest of your document is left alone.

Turn weft on

weft does nothing until a document calls weft::weft_setup(). The smallest way is the document’s own front matter:

---
title: "Creek monitoring"
output: html_document
knitr:
  opts_knit:
    weft: !expr weft::weft_setup()
---

A Quarto document needs engine: knitr in its front matter as well, so that knitr runs it. library(weft) in a chunk does not turn weft on: it only attaches the package. The other ways to turn weft on, and the installers that write them for you, are in vignette("setup", package = "weft").

Once weft is on, inline R in the document can call claim(), plural(), u(), glue_vec(), dict_glossary() and the fmt_*() functions without weft::. Call other weft functions, such as of_n() or weft_str(), as weft::of_n(), or attach the package with library(weft) in a chunk.

A first document

This R Markdown document summarises three turbidity readings.

---
title: "Creek monitoring"
output: html_document
knitr:
  opts_knit:
    weft: !expr weft::weft_setup()
---

```{r data}
sites <- c("Upper", "Middle", "Lower")
turbidity <- c(Upper = 4.2, Middle = 7.9, Lower = 12.6)
n_high <- sum(turbidity > 10)
change <- -0.084
```

We sampled `r length(sites)`{.word} sites: `r sites`{.and}.
Mean turbidity was `r mean(turbidity)`{.num} NTU, and
[no site | one site | # sites]{n="n_high"} read above the trigger.
Turbidity [rose by # | fell by #]{.pct sign="change"} since last year.
The highest reading was `r claim(max(turbidity), . < 50)`{.num} NTU,
at `r names(which.max(turbidity))`.

The paragraph renders as:

We sampled three sites: Upper, Middle and Lower. Mean turbidity was 8.2 NTU,
and one site read above the trigger. Turbidity fell by 8.4% since last year.
The highest reading was 12.6 NTU, at Lower.

Each construct did one job:

  • {.word} spelled the count, and {.and} joined the names.
  • {.num} rounded the mean to the project’s default of one decimal place.
  • The n span chose “one site” because n_high is 1. With no reading above 10 it prints “no site”, and with two it prints “2 sites”.
  • The sign span chose “fell by” because change is negative, and printed its size as a percentage in place of #.
  • claim() checked that the highest reading is below 50 and returned it unchanged for {.num} to print.
  • The last value has no attribute block, so it printed as knitr prints it.

When the reading at Lower is 9.6 instead, the same source renders as:

We sampled three sites: Upper, Middle and Lower. Mean turbidity was 7.2 NTU,
and no site read above the trigger. Turbidity fell by 8.4% since last year.
The highest reading was 9.6 NTU, at Lower.

The words changed with the data. Nobody edited the sentence.

When a check fails

Suppose a storm pushes the reading at Lower to 61.0. The claim that the highest reading is below 50 is now false, and the render stops with this message:

weft: 1 claim failed
  storm.Rmd:20  `r claim(max(turbidity), . < 50)`
      . < 50 was FALSE (value 61)
Read each sentence. If FALSE is right, rewrite the sentence.
Do not loosen a claim to clear this.

A failed check does not stop the knit at once. weft collects every failure in the document, then fails the render once, with each failure’s file and line. Read each sentence the report names and decide which is wrong: the sentence, the check or the data.

A value that cannot be printed is collected the same way. An NA given to {.num} is a “no value” failure, and an error in a construct’s expression is reported with its line.

Draft mode

While you write, you may want to see the whole document even though a check fails. Set the environment variable WEFT_DRAFT=1, or put draft: true in the project’s _weft.yml. In draft mode the render finishes, the failures are listed in the knit log, and each failed construct carries a visible marker:

The highest reading was 61<<weft: failed claim, line 20>> NTU, at Lower.

Every marker starts with <<weft:, so you can search for it. Draft mode covers the render only. verify() refuses to run in draft mode, and the commit gate ignores it.

If weft is not on

A document whose constructs are never resolved does not print plausible text. Without weft_setup(), the attribute blocks print as text, for example “We sampled 3{.word} sites”, and a claim() call stops the knit because claim is not found. In a set-up project the weft-check filter also fails the render on any leftover construct.

weft from R code

Each formatter class has a function of the same name, for use in chunks, plots and tables:

library(weft)
fmt_num(8.2333)
#> <weft_text>
#> [1] "8.2"
fmt_word(3)
#> <weft_text>
#> [1] "three"
fmt_and(c("Upper", "Middle", "Lower"))
#> <weft_text>
#> [1] "Upper, Middle and Lower"
fmt_pct(-0.084)
#> <weft_text>
#> [1] "−8.4%"

plural() is the function form of an n span:

plural(1, "a site", "# sites")
#> [1] "a site"
plural(4, "a site", "# sites")
#> [1] "4 sites"

weft_str() resolves weft markup in a string, for text that no chunk option reaches, such as a table caption:

n_sites <- 3
weft_str("Turbidity at `r n_sites`{.word} sites.")
#> [1] "Turbidity at three sites."

Outside a knit, a failed check stops at once with an error:

claim(61, . < 50)
#> Error:
#> ! weft: 1 failed claim
#>   check `. < 50` failed (value: 61)
